You will now start writing the code for this game in a few steps. As an initial step, you will write the code that starts the program and sets the ‘starting’ state. Then, you will see how to set the 'playing' state (position all graphic elements) after Start button is clicked. You then write the code to move the ball to the bottom of the screen, shift man (using a mouse click or keyboard key), and check whether man is able to capture the ball. During the code development process, you will modify certain procedures repeatedly before reaching the final definition.

Step 6

After the game difficulty level is set, the next step is to click on Start button so the game can start. So, you need a code to get from the "Starting" state to the "Playing" state. When Start button is clicked on the "Starting" state, these steps need to be carried out:

  • Change StatusGame to "Playing".
  • Clean the screen.
  • Initialize the score and remaining time.
  • Place man on the bottom area of the screen.
  • Place bird and ball on the top area of the screen randomly.
  • Drop ball.

 

There is a lot that needs to be done here, you will do it step by step. First, you will initialize the variables and position man at the bottom of the screen.

The Score tells how many balls man caught. PanelGame is a graphics region which is a place for games.

Step 26

When the ball approaches the bottom of the screen, you need to see if man can catch it. The code to check this is in the Tick event procedure of timerGame . You need to do two things:

  • Check whether the ball is caught. If so, the ball is cleared and the score is incremented and the bird and ball appear again at a random location at the top of the screen.
  • Check whether the ball has reached the same vertical position as man and has not been caught. If yes, bird and ball reappears.

How do you know when man catches ball? You need to see if man's graphics collide with the ball graphics. The inspection could not be carried out until the ball overlaps man. This happens when: BallY + BallH> ManY .

 

You will use a boolean variable ( Passed ) to see this. After this condition is met, you can see that man collides with ball (or catches ball) when:

 

ManX + ManW> BallX and ManX <BallX + BallW .

 

This says that the right side of man must be "more right" than the left side of the ball and the left side of man must be "more left" than the right side of the bal. Another boolean variable ( Collision ) is used to check this condition.

 

Declare these two new variables:

 

1

bool Passed, Collision;

private void timerGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

   ClearBall();

    BallY = BallY + BallSpeed;

    PanelGame.DrawImage(picBall.Image, BallX, BallY);

 

    //Move man

    ClearMan();

    if (KeyPressed == "Left" || ButtonClicked == "Left " )

    {

        ManX = ManX - ManDeltaX;

        if (ManX < 0)

            ManX = 0;

    }

 

    else if (KeyPressed == "Right" || ButtonClicked == "Right " )

    {

        ManX = ManX + ManDeltaX;

        if (ManX > (pnlGame.Width - ManW))

            ManX = pnlGame.Width - ManW;

     }

    PanelGame.DrawImage(picMan.Image, ManX, ManY);

 

    //Checks whether ball collides with or passes man

    Passed = false ;

    Collision = false ;

    if (BallY + BallH > ManY)

    {

        Passed = true ;

        if (ManX + ManW > BallX && ManX < BallX + BallW)

            Collision = true ;

        if (Passed)

            if (Collision)

                Score += 1;

 

        ClearBird();

        ClearBall();

        PlaceBirdAndBall();

    }

    DisplayTimeScore();

}

private void timerGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

   ClearBall();

    BallY = BallY + BallSpeed;

    PanelGame.DrawImage(picBall.Image, BallX, BallY);

 

    //Move man

    ClearMan();

    if (KeyPressed == "Left" || ButtonClicked == "Left " )

    {

        ManX = ManX - ManDeltaX;

        if (ManX < 0)

            ManX = 0;

    }

 

    else if (KeyPressed == "Right" || ButtonClicked == "Right " )

    {

        ManX = ManX + ManDeltaX;

        if (ManX > (pnlGame.Width - ManW))

            ManX = pnlGame.Width - ManW;

     }

    PanelGame.DrawImage(picMan.Image, ManX, ManY);

 

    //Checks whether ball collides with or passes man

    Passed = false ;

    Collision = false ;

    if (BallY + BallH > ManY)

    {

        Passed = true ;

        if (ManX + ManW > BallX && ManX < BallX + BallW)

            Collision = true ;

        if (Passed)

            if (Collision)

                Score += 1;

 

        ClearBird();

        ClearBall();

        PlaceBirdAndBall();

    }

 

    //Updates time

    RemainingTime = RemainingTime - timerGame.Interval;

    DisplayTimeScore();

 

    if (RemainingTime == 0)

    {

        ClearBird();

        ClearBall();

        ClearMan();

        timerGame.Stop();

        MessageBox.Show( "You successfully catch "

            + Score.ToString() + " balls." , "Game Over" );

        StatusGame = "Starting" ;

    }

}

 

In this new code, with each Tick event, RemainingTime will be decremented by the Interval . After RemainingTime is zero, then the graphical elements (bird, ball, and man) will be removed from the screen, the timer is deactivated, and the result is displayed in a message box.

using System;

using System.Collections.Generic;

using System.ComponentModel;

using System.Data;

using System.Drawing;

using System.Linq;

using System.Text;

using System.Threading.Tasks;

using System.Windows.Forms;

 

namespace Horse_Racing

{

    public partial class FormCatchingBall : Form

    {

        int Difficulty;

        String StatusGame;

 

        int RemainingTime;

        int Score;

        Graphics PanelGame;

 

        int ManW, ManH, ManX, ManY, ManDeltaX;

 

        int BirdW, BirdH, BirdX;

        int BallW, BallH, BallX, BallY;

        Random MyRandom = new Random();

        int BallSpeed;

 

        String KeyPressed = "Empty" ;

        String ButtonClicked = "Empty" ;

 

        bool Passed, Collision;

 

        private void timerGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            ClearBall();

            BallY = BallY + BallSpeed;

            PanelGame.DrawImage(picBall.Image, BallX, BallY);

 

            //Move man

            ClearMan();

            if (KeyPressed == "Left" || ButtonClicked == "Left" )

            {

                ManX = ManX - ManDeltaX;

                if (ManX < 0)

                    ManX = 0;

            }

 

            else if (KeyPressed == "Right" || ButtonClicked == "Right" )

            {

                ManX = ManX + ManDeltaX;

                if (ManX > (pnlGame.Width - ManW))

                    ManX = pnlGame.Width - ManW;

 

            }

            PanelGame.DrawImage(picMan.Image, ManX, ManY);

 

            //Checks whether ball collides with or passes man

            Passed = false ;

            Collision = false ;

            if (BallY + BallH > ManY)

            {

                Passed = true ;

                if (ManX + ManW > BallX && ManX < BallX + BallW)

                    Collision = true ;

                if (Passed)

                    if (Collision)

                        Score += 1;

 

                ClearBird();

                ClearBall();

                PlaceBirdAndBall();

            }

 

            //Updates time

            RemainingTime = RemainingTime - timerGame.Interval;

            DisplayTimeScore();

 

            if (RemainingTime == 0)

            {

                ClearBird();

                ClearBall();

                ClearMan();

 

                timerGame.Stop();

                MessageBox.Show( "You successfully catch "

                    + Score.ToString() + " balls." , "Game Over" );

                StatusGame = "Starting" ;

            }

        }

 

        private void ClearBird()

        {

            PanelGame.FillRectangle(Brushes.Gold, BirdX, 0, BirdW + 30, BirdH + 30);

        }

 

        private void ClearMan()

        {

            PanelGame.FillRectangle(Brushes.Gold, ManX, ManY, ManW + 50, ManH);

        }

 

        private void FormCatchingBall_KeyDown( object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

        {

            //Check which arry key is pressed to move man

            if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Left)

                KeyPressed = "Left" ;

            else if (e.KeyCode == Keys.Right)

                KeyPressed = "Right" ;

        }

 

        private void FormCatchingBall_KeyUp( object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

        {

            KeyPressed = "Empty" ;

        }

 

        private void pnlGame_MouseDown( object sender, MouseEventArgs e)

        {

            if (e.Button == MouseButtons.Left)

                ButtonClicked = "Left" ;

            else if (e.Button == MouseButtons.Right)

                ButtonClicked = "Right" ;

        }

 

        private void pnlGame_MouseUp( object sender, MouseEventArgs e)

        {

            ButtonClicked = "Empty" ;

        }

 

        private void ClearBall()

        {

            PanelGame. FillRectangle(Brushes.Gold, BallX, BallY, BallW + 5, BallH + 5);

        }

 

        private void btnStop_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (StatusGame == "Starting" )

                this .Close();

            else

            {

                //Stop button clicked when game played

                timerGame.Stop();

                StatusGame = "Starting" ;

                MessageBox.Show( "You quit the game." , "Game Over" );

                ClearMan();

                ClearBird();

                ClearBall();

            }

        }

 

        private void btnStart_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            //Start button clicked

            StatusGame = "Playing" ;

            lblInstruction.Visible = false ;

            PanelGame = pnlGame.CreateGraphics();

            PanelGame.Clear(Color.Gold); //time/score

            RemainingTime = 60 * 1000;  //milliseconds

            Score = 0;

 

            DisplayTimeScore();

 

            //Man

            ManW = picMan.Width;

            ManH = picMan.Height;

            ManDeltaX = 10;

            ManX = 375;

            ManY = pnlGame.Height - ManH;

            PanelGame.DrawImage(picMan.Image, ManX, ManY);

 

            //Bird

            BirdW = picBird.Width;

            BirdH = picBird.Height;

 

            //Ball

            BallW = picBall.Width + 10;

            BallH = picBall.Height;

 

            PlaceBirdAndBall();

 

            //Start timer

            BallSpeed = Convert.ToInt32(0.5 * Difficulty) + 5;

            timerGame.Start();

            pnlGame.Focus();

        }

 

        private void PlaceBirdAndBall()

        {

            BirdX = MyRandom.Next(pnlGame.Width - BirdW);

            PanelGame.DrawImage(picBird.Image, BirdX, 0);

            BallX = BirdX + Convert.ToInt32(0.5 * (BirdW - BallW));

            BallY = BirdH + 10;

            PanelGame.DrawImage(picBall.Image, BallX, BallY);

        }

 

        private void DisplayTimeScore()

        {

            lblTime.Text = (RemainingTime / 1000).ToString();

            lblScore.Text = Score.ToString();

        }

 

        public FormCatchingBall ()

        {

            InitializeComponent();

        }

 

 

        private void FormCatchingBall_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            this .KeyPreview = true ;

            //Catching Ball Game

            Difficulty = 1;

            StatusGame = "Starting" ;

 

            lblInstruction.Text = "CATCHING BALL GAME \n\n" ;

            lblInstruction.Text += "In this game, you will try to \n" +

                "catch as many as possible fallen ball." ;

            lblInstruction.Text += "\n\nUse the left and right arrow key " +

                "or the left and right mouse buttons to " +

                "move man under the fallen ball." ;

 

            lblInstruction.Text += "\n\nChoose the game difficulty level by pressing " +

                "the left or right mouse button." ;

            lblInstruction.Text += "\n\nClick Start button to start the game." +

                "\nClick Stop button to stop the game." ;

 

            lblDifficulty.Text = Difficulty.ToString();

 

            PanelGame = pnlGame.CreateGraphics();

 

        }

 

        private void btnLeft_Click_1( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (StatusGame == "Starting" ) // Decreases difficulty level

            {

                Difficulty -= 1;

                if (Difficulty < 1)

                    Difficulty = 1;

 

                lblDifficulty.Text = Difficulty.ToString();

            }

        }

 

        private void btnRight_Click_1( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (StatusGame == "Starting" ) // Increasesdifficulty level

            {

                Difficulty += 1;

                if (Difficulty > 10)

                    Difficulty = 10;

 

                lblDifficulty.Text = Difficulty.ToString();

            }

        }

    }

}

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

TUTORIAL 6

SMART TIC TAC TOE

 

 

In this tutorial, you will build Smart Tic Tac Toe game. That said, this is the first game ever programmed on a computer and one that had been programmed by Bill Gates himself when he was a teenager while attending Lakeside School in Seattle. The aim of this game is to win the game on a 3 x 3 grid with the victory of three identical symbols (X or O) on horizontal, diagonal, or vertical lines. The players will play alternately. In this game given two game options: player 1 against player 2 or human player against computer. A smart but simple strategy will be developed for computer logic to be a formidable opponent for humans.

 

Description

Run the project (press <F5>). The game will be displayed in the 'stop' state, the grid will be cleared and waiting for you to choose game options (one or two players and, if one player, who plays first and how smart the computer will oppose).

 

Figure 6.1 All controls used in Smart Tic Tac Toe game project

 

 

Figure 6.2 The game is at “stop” state

 

You can choose the two players option and then press Start Game button:

 

Figure 6.3 User chooses two players option

 

In addition, you can choose the option of one player with a random computer or a smart computer opponent:

 

Figure 6.4 User chooses one player option

 

 

Tutorial Steps

Step 1

You will build Smart Tic Tac Toe game project. Start a new project in Visual C#. Once created, you are advised to save the project immediately with the name you choose. This will create the folders and file structure that your project requires.

 

Figure 6.5 All controls user and their positions form

 

You need 14 label controls (with the AutoSize property set to False so that the size can be changed and the BorderStyle property temporarily set to FixedSingle to see edges) on the left side of the form. Place the three group boxes on the right side, along with the two control buttons. Place two radio button controls in each group box. The form will look as shown in Figure 6.5.

 

Label controls are used to display messages, to display symbols (X and O), and to form a grid. The radio buttons are used to set game options. Buttons (one to start the game and one to end the game) are used to control game operations.

When finished, the form will look like as shown in Figure 6.6.

 

This completes the form design. You will start writing the code for this game. You will write the code in several stages. As a first step, you will write the code that starts the game and sets the 'stop' state. Then, you will write the code for the 'playing' state after Start Game button is clicked. During the code development process, you will modify certain methods several times before arriving at the final process.

 

Step 3

Every time you start a project, a number of initializations are needed. In this case, all initializations are placed in the Load event method of the form.

 

To simplify the task, you will specify an array of controls ( LabelArr ) for the nine label controls that are used to display X and O marks on the grid. This array is defined in the form-level declaration:

 

1

Label[] LabelArr = new Label[9];

 

Figure 6.7 The game is in “stop” state

 

Assignments are performed in the Load event method of FormTicTacToe . You also create a message in lblMessage control and clear the label controls that display the symbol. Finally, you want the game to be initialized in Two Players mode so you disable two group boxes related to options for single player mode:

private void FormTicTacToe_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    // Fills array

    LabelArr[0] = lblBox1;

    LabelArr[1] = lblBox2;

    LabelArr[2] = lblBox3;

    LabelArr[3] = lblBox4;

    LabelArr[4] = lblBox5;

    LabelArr[5] = lblBox6;

    LabelArr[6] = lblBox7;

    LabelArr[7] = lblBox8;

    LabelArr[8] = lblBox9;

 

    // Clears labels

    for ( int i = 0; i < 9; i++)

        LabelArr[i].Text = "" ;

 

    lblMessage.Text = "Game Stopped" ;

    grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

    grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

}

 

 

Step 4

Save and run the project to make sure everything works correctly, as shown in Figure 6.8.

 

Step 5

As desired, the game is initialized in Two Players mode. You have two choices at this point: clicking btnStartStop (Start Game button) or clicking btnExit . You can also change to One Player mode. You will handle this later.

 

The code to exit the program is quite simple. Click event from the control btnExit :

 

1

2

3

4

private void btnExit_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    this .Close();

}

 

It only says that whenever the Exit button is clicked, the project will close. Add this code to your project.

 

The code for the btnStartStop button is much more complex. You will write it in several stages. First, you will switch the code to shift the game from the stop state to the playing state.

 

Step 6

When user clicks Start Game button in the "stop" state, several things happen to switch the Tic Tac Toe game to the "play" state:

  • Change Text property of btnStartStop to Stop Game .
  • Disable group boxes (do not allow selection of options when playing).
  • Disable Exit button.
  • Set X's turn (because the X symbol is always used first).
  • Clear label controls that display symbols.
  • Allow user to enter symbols on the grid.

 

You create three variables in the form-level declaration to help track a number of situations in the game:

 

1

2

3

bool XTurn;

bool Clickable = false ;

int NumberOfClick;

 

If XTurn is true , then the X symbol will appear, otherwise the O symbol will appear. Clickable is used to determine whether user can click on label controls. If this variable is true , if the game is in progress. Instead, it is false (initial value) when the game stops. NumberOfClick tracks how many grid labels have been clicked (maximum 9).

 

Figure 6.9 The game is in “playing” state

 

The code for the Click event of btnStartStop that implements the steps above is given below:

private void btnStartStop_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    btnStartStop.Text = "Stop Game" ;

    grpPlayer.Enabled = false ;

    grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

    grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

    btnExit.Enabled = false ;

    XTurn = true ;

    lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

 

    // Clears LabelArr

    for ( int i = 0; i < 9; i++)

        LabelArr[i].Text = "" ;

 

    Clickable = true ;

    NumberOfClick = 0;

}

 

 

Step 7

Save and run the project. Click Start Game button and the game will switch to the "playing" state, as shown in Figure 6.9.

 

The game waits until the first player clicks on one of the grid locations (you will write the code in a minute). Notice Stop Game button doesn't do anything for now.

 

Step 8

When user clicks Stop Game button in "playing" state with two-players mode, several things must occur to switch Tic Tac Toe game to the "stop" state:

  • Change the Text property of btnStartStop to Start Game .
  • Display “Game Ends” message.
  • Enable grpPlayer .
  • Enable grpFirst and grpComputer with one player mode.
  • Enable Exit button.
  • Set Clickable to false .

 

The modified code that performs these steps is placed in the Click event method of the btnStartStop control:

private void btnStartStop_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (btnStartStop.Text == "Start Game" )

    {

        btnStartStop.Text = "Stop Game" ;

        grpPlayer.Enabled = false ;

        grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

        grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

        btnExit.Enabled = false ;

        XTurn = true ;

        lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

 

        // Clears LabelArr

        for ( int i = 0; i < 9; i++)

            LabelArr[i].Text = "" ;

 

        Clickable = true ;

        NumberOfClick = 0;

 

    else

    {

        btnStartStop.Text = "Start Game" ;

        lblMessage.Text = "Game Ends" ;

        grpPlayer.Enabled = true ;

 

        if (rdoOnePlayer.Checked)

        {

            grpFirst.Enabled = true ;

            grpComputer.Enabled = true ;

        }

        btnExit.Enabled = true ;

        Clickable = false ;

    }

}

 

 

Step 9

Save and run project. You can now move from the "stop" to the "playing" state and vice versa. When stop, make sure the group boxes are enabled for one and two player options.

 

Figure 6.10 User now can move from the "stop" to the "playing" state and vice versa

 

You will write the code for the two player option, by first writing the code to display the symbol on the grid.

 

Step 10

In the Tic Tac Toe game with a two player option, when a player clicks on a box on the grid, an appropriate symbol (X or O) will appear. After that, you then need to see if someone wins the game. If there is no win, and there is still an empty box, the turn switch to another player.

 

So, when a grid box is clicked, these steps need to be done:

  • Verify that there is no symbol on the grid before.
  • Increment NumberOfClick .
  • Place the right symbol (X if XTurn is true , otherwise O).
  • Switch turn to the next player (not required if there is a win or a draw).
  • Check for winning. If there is a win, the winner is announced and the game is stopped.
  • Check if NumberOfClick = 9 (board is full but no win). If yes, the draw is announced and the game is stopped.

 

The code to perform these steps will be placed in the method named lblBox_Click . This method was created to handle the Click event for the nine label controls used on the grid ( lblBox1 , lblBox2 , lblBox3 , lblBox4 , lblBox5 , lblBox6 , lblBox7 , lblBox8 , and lblBox9 .

 

Add this method ( lblBox_Click ) to your project. This implements the steps needed to receive symbols on the grid:

private void lblBox_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    String WhoWin = "" ;

    int i;

 

    if (Clickable)

    {

        // See which box clicked

        Label BoxClicked;

        BoxClicked = (Label) sender;

 

        // Last digit is the number extracted

        i = Convert.ToInt32(

            BoxClicked. Name[BoxClicked.Name.Length - 1].ToString()) - 1;

 

        // If it has been clicked, exit

        if (LabelArr[i].Text != "" )

            return ;

 

        NumberOfClick++;

 

        if (XTurn)

        {

            LabelArr[i].Text = "X" ;

            XTurn = false ;

            lblMessage.Text = "O's Turn" ;

        }

        else

        {

            LabelArr[i].Text = "O" ;

            XTurn = true ;

            lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

        }

 

        if (WhoWin != "" )

        {

            lblMessage.Text = WhoWin + " wins” ;

private String CheckWinning()

{

    String Winner = "" ;

    int [] BoxNumber = new int [3];

    String[] Symbol = new String[3];

 

    // Checks all possible winning

    for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

    {

        for ( int j = 0; j < 3; j++)

        {

            BoxNumber[j] =

                Convert.ToInt32(WinningArr[i][j].ToString());

            Symbol[j] = LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].Text;

        }

 

        if (Symbol[0] == Symbol[1] && Symbol[0] == Symbol[2] &&

           Symbol[1] == Symbol[2] && Symbol[0] != "" )

        {

            // There is a winner

            Winner = Symbol[0];

            for ( int j = 0; j < 3; j++)

                LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].BackColor = Color.Red;

        }

    }

    return (Winner);

}

 

This code checks all possible winning. If all symbols on horizontal lines, vertical lines, or diagonal lines are the same symbols, then the background color of the line is changed to blue. BoxNumber array contains the indexes of LabelArr array for each possible win.

Step 20

You have experienced the fun part of this game project. How do you make computer a smart opponent? In every game where a computer becomes a human opponent, you need to write down rules that give the computer intelligence. Many computer opponents that can not be conquered. For example, in chess games, computer beats human more often than vice versa.

 

So how do you make computer as a better opponent in this Tic Tac Toe game? You certainly design how logic when human plays it. So, for computer to be intelligent player, programmer also needs to be intelligent. This generally requires practice and learning. For the Tic Tac Toe game, you can develop a simple, but very smart strategy.

 

When it becomes the computer's turn, what movements need to be done? The rules used here are:

  • If the computer can win the game in one move, then the move must be made and the game ends. So, if there is one line with two symbols given by the computer and an empty box, then the empty space must be given a symbol by the computer.
  • If the computer can block with one move, then the move must be done and the opponent will not be able to win the game in the next move. So, if there is a line with two symbols given by human and an empty box, then the empty space must be taken over by computer by giving it a symbol.
  • If there is no possibility of winning or blocking that is possible, then the movement is carried out in this order: the middle box, one of the four corner boxes, or one of the four side squares.

 

You might ask about the third step above, why the order is important. Remember that there are 8 possible ways to win the game (3 horizontal, 3 vertical, and 2 diagonal). The square box is involved in 4 possible wins, the corner box is involved in three possible wins, and the side box is involved in only two wins.

 

You will implement these steps. The following is a modified version of the ComputerTurn method that implements this smart logic:

private void ComputerTurn()

{

    int BoxSelected;

    int i, n;

 

    int j, k;

    String ComputerSymbol, PlayerSymbol, WhichSymbol;

    int [] BoxNumber = new int [3];

    String[] Symbols = new String[3];

    int EmptyBox;

    int [] BestMove = { 4, 0, 2, 6, 8, 1, 3, 5, 7 };

 

    if (rdoRandom.Checked)

    {

        // Random logic

        // Put symbol on N-th empty box

        n = MyRandom.Next(9 - NumberOfClick) + 1;

        i = 0;

 

        for (BoxSelected = 0; BoxSelected < 9; BoxSelected++)

        {

            if (LabelArr[BoxSelected].Text == "" )

                i++;

            if (i == n)

                break ;

        }

 

        // Put symbol on BoxSelected

        lblBox_Click(LabelArr[BoxSelected], null );

    }

    else

    {

        // Smart computer

        // Determines who has what symbol

        if (rdoComputerFirst.Checked)

        {

            ComputerSymbol = "X" ;

            PlayerSymbol = "O" ;

        }

        else

        {

            ComputerSymbol = "O" ;

            PlayerSymbol = "X" ;

        }

 

        //Step 1 (K = 1) - checks winning: if there is one line with

        //two Symbols given by the computer And an empty box

        //Step 2 (K = 2) - checks blocking: if there is a line with

        //two Symbols given by human And an empty box

        for (k = 1; k <= 2; k++)

        {

            if (k == 1)

                WhichSymbol = ComputerSymbol;

            else

                WhichSymbol = PlayerSymbol;

 

            for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)

            {

                n = 0;

                EmptyBox = 0;

 

                for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)

                {

                    BoxNumber[j] =

                      Convert.ToInt32(WinningArr[i][j].ToString());

                    Symbols[j] = LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].Text;

 

                    if (Symbols[j] == WhichSymbol)

                        n++;

                    else if (Symbols[j] == "" )

                        EmptyBox = BoxNumber[j];

                }

 

                if (n == 2 && EmptyBox != 0)

                {

                    //Give symbol on empty box to win

                    //(K = 1) or to block(K = 2)

                    lblBox_Click(LabelArr[EmptyBox], null );

                    return ;

                }

            }

        }

 

        // Step 3: Find the best movement

        for (i = 0; i < 9; i++)

        {

            if (LabelArr[BestMove[i]].Text == "" )

            {

                lblBox_Click(LabelArr[BestMove[i]], null );

                return ;

            }

        }

    }

}

 

In this smart logic, you find out whether the computer has X or O. Step 1 and 2 of computer logic are done in a for loop with k as an index. In that loop, all possible wins are sought on a line with 2 identical symbols and an empty box. For k = 1, you look for the computer symbol and an empty box, which gives the computer the next move. For k = 2, you look for a human symbol and an empty box, which gives the computer a blockage in the next move.

 

If either step 1 or step 2 is successful, you move to step 3. The next best move is done in the order in BestMove array. In step 3, you read this array, look for available empty boxes and move there.

            XTurn = false ;

        }

        else

        {

            LabelArr[i].Text = "O" ;

            XTurn = true ;

            lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

        }

 

        // Who wins?

        WhoWin = CheckWinning();

 

        if (WhoWin != "" )

        {

            WinSound.Play();

            lblMessage.Text = WhoWin + " wins” ;

            GameOver = true ;

            btnStartStop.PerformClick();

            return ;

        }

        else if (NumberOfClick == 9)

        {

            // Draw

            DrawSound.Play();

            lblMessage.Text = "Game is draw!" ;

            GameOver = true ;

            btnStartStop.PerformClick();

            return ;

        }

 

        if (rdoOnePlayer.Checked)

            if ((XTurn && rdoComputerFirst.Checked) ||

                   (!XTurn && rdoYouFirst.Checked))

                ComputerTurn();

 

    }

}

Save and run the project. Now, you have the full version of the Smart Tic Tac Toe game.

using System;

using System.Collections.Generic;

using System.ComponentModel;

using System.Data;

using System.Drawing;

using System.Linq;

using System.Text;

using System.Threading.Tasks;

using System.Windows.Forms;

 

namespace Tic_Tac_Toe

{

    public partial class FormTicTacToe : Form

    {

        Label[] LabelArr = new Label[9];

        bool XTurn;

        bool Clickable = false ;

        int NumberOfClick;

        String[] WinningArr = new String[8];

        bool GameOver;

        Random MyRandom = new Random();

 

        System.Media.SoundPlayer DrawSound;

        System.Media.SoundPlayer WinSound;

 

        public FormTicTacToe ()

        {

            InitializeComponent();

        }

 

        private void FormTicTacToe_Load( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            // Fills array

            LabelArr[0] = lblBox1;

            LabelArr[1] = lblBox2;

            LabelArr[2] = lblBox3;

            LabelArr[3] = lblBox4;

            LabelArr[4] = lblBox5;

            LabelArr[5] = lblBox6;

            LabelArr[6] = lblBox7;

            LabelArr[7] = lblBox8;

            LabelArr[8] = lblBox9;

 

            // Possible winnings

            WinningArr[0] = "012" ;

            WinningArr[1] = "345" ;

            WinningArr[2] = "678" ;

            WinningArr[3] = "036" ;

            WinningArr[4] = "147" ;

            WinningArr[5] = "258" ;

            WinningArr[6] = "048" ;

            WinningArr[7] = "246" ;

 

            // Clears labels

            for ( int i = 0; i < 9; i++)

                LabelArr[i].Text = "" ;

 

            lblMessage.Text = "Game Stopped" ;

            grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

            grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

 

            DrawSound = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath +

                "\\draw.wav" );

            WinSound = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(Application.StartupPath +

                "\\win.wav" );

        }

 

        private void btnExit_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            this .Close();

        }

 

        private void btnStartStop_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            if (btnStartStop.Text == "Start Game" )

            {

                btnStartStop.Text = "Stop Game" ;

                grpPlayer.Enabled = false ;

                grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

                grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

                btnExit.Enabled = false ;

                XTurn = true ;

                lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

 

                // Clears LabelArr

                for ( int i = 0; i < 9; i++)

                {

                    LabelArr[i].Text = "" ;

                    LabelArr[i].BackColor = Color.White;

                }

                Clickable = true ;

                NumberOfClick = 0;

                GameOver = false ;

 

                if (rdoComputerFirst.Checked && rdoOnePlayer.Checked)

                    ComputerTurn();

            }

            else

            {

                btnStartStop.Text = "Start Game" ;

                if (!GameOver)

                    lblMessage.Text = "Game Ends" ;

                grpPlayer.Enabled = true ;

 

                if (rdoOnePlayer.Checked)

                {

                    grpFirst.Enabled = true ;

                    grpComputer.Enabled = true ;

                }

                btnExit.Enabled = true ;

                Clickable = false ;

            }

        }

 

        private void lblBox_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            String WhoWin = "" ;

            int i;

 

            if (Clickable)

            {

                // See which box clicked

                Label BoxClicked;

                BoxClicked = (Label) sender;

 

                // Last digit is the number extracted

                i = Convert.ToInt32(

                    BoxClicked.Name[BoxClicked.Name.Length - 1].ToString()) - 1;

 

                // If it has been clicked, exit

                if (LabelArr[i].Text != "" )

                    return ;

 

                NumberOfClick++;

 

                if (XTurn)

                {

                    LabelArr[i].Text = "X" ;

                    XTurn = false ;

                    lblMessage.Text = "O's Turn" ;

                }

                else

                {

                    LabelArr[i].Text = "O" ;

                    XTurn = true ;

                    lblMessage.Text = "X's Turn" ;

                }

 

                // Who wins?

                WhoWin = CheckWinning();

 

                if (WhoWin != "" )

                {

                    WinSound.Play();

                    lblMessage.Text = WhoWin + " wins" ;

                    GameOver = true ;

                    btnStartStop.PerformClick();

                    return ;

                }

                else if (NumberOfClick == 9)

                {

                    // Draw

                    DrawSound.Play();

                    lblMessage.Text = "Game is draw!" ;

                    GameOver = true ;

                    btnStartStop.PerformClick();

                    return ;

                }

 

                if (rdoOnePlayer.Checked)

                    if ((XTurn && rdoComputerFirst.Checked) ||

                           (!XTurn && rdoYouFirst.Checked))

                        ComputerTurn();

            }

        }

 

        private String CheckWinning()

        {

            String Winner = "" ;

            int [] BoxNumber = new int [3];

            String[] Symbol = new String[3];

 

            // Checks all possible winning

            for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++)

            {

                for ( int j = 0; j < 3; j++)

                {

                    BoxNumber[j] = Convert.ToInt32(WinningArr[i][j].ToString());

                    Symbol[j] = LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].Text;

                }

 

                if (Symbol[0] == Symbol[1] && Symbol[0] == Symbol[2] &&

                    Symbol[1] == Symbol[2] && Symbol[0] != "" )

                {

                    // There is a winner

                    Winner = Symbol[0];

                    for ( int j = 0; j < 3; j++)

                        LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].BackColor = Color.Red;

                }

            }

            return (Winner);

        }

 

        private void rdoSatuPemain_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            grpFirst.Enabled = true ;

            grpComputer.Enabled = true ;

        }

 

        private void rdoDuaPemain_CheckedChanged( object sender, EventArgs e)

        {

            grpFirst.Enabled = false ;

            grpComputer.Enabled = false ;

        }

 

        private void ComputerTurn()

        {

            int BoxSelected;

            int i, n;

 

            int j, k;

            String ComputerSymbol, PlayerSymbol, WhichSymbol;

            int [] BoxNumber = new int [3];

            String[] Symbols = new String[3];

            int EmptyBox;

            int [] BestMove = { 4, 0, 2, 6, 8, 1, 3, 5, 7 };

 

            if (rdoRandom.Checked)

            {

                // Random logic

                // Put symbol on N-th empty box

                n = MyRandom.Next(9 - NumberOfClick) + 1;

                i = 0;

 

                for (BoxSelected = 0; BoxSelected < 9; BoxSelected++)

                {

                    if (LabelArr[BoxSelected].Text == "" )

                        i++;

                    if (i == n)

                        break ;

                }

 

                // Put symbol on BoxSelected

                lblBox_Click(LabelArr[BoxSelected], null );

            }

            else

            {

                // Smart computer

                // Determines who has what symbol

                if (rdoComputerFirst.Checked)

                {

                    ComputerSymbol = "X" ;

                    PlayerSymbol = "O" ;

                }

                else

                {

                    ComputerSymbol = "O" ;

                    PlayerSymbol = "X" ;

                }

 

                //Step 1 (K = 1) - checks winning: if there is one line with

                //two Symbols given by the computer And an empty box

                //Step 2 (K = 2) - checks blocking: if there is a line with

                //two Symbols given by human And an empty box

 

                for (k = 1; k <= 2; k++)

                {

                    if (k == 1)

                        WhichSymbol = ComputerSymbol;

                    else

                        WhichSymbol = PlayerSymbol;

 

                    for (i = 0; i < 8; i++)

                    {

                        n = 0;

                        EmptyBox = 0;

 

                        for (j = 0; j < 3; j++)

                        {

                            BoxNumber[j] =

                                Convert.ToInt32(WinningArr[i][j].ToString());

                            Symbols[j] = LabelArr[BoxNumber[j]].Text;

 

                            if (Symbols[j] == WhichSymbol)

                                n++;

                            else if (Symbols[j] == "" )

                                EmptyBox = BoxNumber[j];

                        }

 

                        if (n == 2 && EmptyBox != 0)

                        {

                            //Give symbol on empty box to win

                            //(K = 1) or to block(K = 2)

                            lblBox_Click(LabelArr[EmptyBox], null );

                            return ;

                        }

                    }

                }

 

                // Step 3: Find the best movement

                for (i = 0; i < 9; i++)

                {

                    if (LabelArr[BestMove[i]].Text == "" )

                    {

                        lblBox_Click(LabelArr[BestMove[i]], null );

                        return ;

                    }

                }

            }

        }

    }

}

 

 

 

 

 

 

TUTORIAL 7

FIGHTING PLANE

 

 

In this tutorial, you will build Fighting Plane program. This program can be played by two human players or human player versus computer.

 

Description

Start Visual C# and open the project and press <F5> to run it, you will see:

 

Figure 7.1 Fighting Plane game starts

 

Next, press Options button. Choose One . With one player, you can also choose the level of difficulty of the game, as shown in Figure 7.1.

 

Click OK and then click New Game button. Game will start, as shown in Figure 7.2.

 

The controls of the player are done via the keyboard. Player 1 presses A key to move up, Z key to move down, and S key to throw rudal.

 

When you choose Two players from the Options button, this game can be played by two human players. Player 1 presses the same keys, while player 2 presses key K to move up, M to move down, and key J to throw rudal, as shown in Figure 7.3.

 

Figure 7.2 User chooses one player and hard difficulty level

 

 

 

Figure 7.3 User play against computer

 

 

 

 

 

Figure 7.4 Human versus human

 

 

Tutorial Steps

Step 1

You will start building Fighting Plane game project. Start a new project in Visual C#. Place 12 labels, a large control panel, and three control buttons on the form. In the control panel, place a smaller panel with two group box controls and a button control. In the first group box, place 2 radio buttons; in the second box group, place 4 radio buttons. Add two timer controls to the project. Change the size and position of each control so that the form is now as shown in Figure 7.5.

 

All label controls are used for titles and provide scoring and game information. The large panel ( Panel1 ) is the playing field. Three button controls are used to start / stop a program, set options, and exit the program. One timer control is used to control game animation and another is used to represent the computer's decision process. The second control panel ( Panel2 ) is used to select game options. One group box contains radio buttons which are used to select number of players. A group box contains radio buttons to select the level of difficulty of the game, when playing against a computer. A small button is used to close the options panel. The default properties are set for one-player games with the easiest game difficulty.

Step 4

When the game starts, user will choose the options (number of players and the difficulty level of the game). Based on these choices, the form will display different information.

 

When the user clicks Options button ( btnOption ), the following things occur:

  • Disable Exit button.
  • Make pnlOption visible.

Add this procedure to your project. When the project is run and the user clicks on the Options button, the form will be displayed as shown in Figure 7.8.

After the options panel is displayed, the user can choose one or two players and select game difficulty (if playing against computer). You will use an Integer variable named NumberOfPlayer to save number of players and an Integer variable with the name Difficulty to save the selected difficulty level. Step 7

If the one player radio button ( rdoOnePlayer ) is selected, user will play against computer and the following happens:

  • Set NumberOfPlayer to 1.
  • Set Text property of lblPlayer1 to You: .
  • Set Text property of lblPlayer2 to Computer: .
  • Make lblInstructionPlayer2 control invisible.
  • Enable grpDifficulty .

 

If the two player ( rdoTwoPlayers ) radio button is selected, the user will play against another human and the following happens:

  • Set NumberOfPlayer to 2.
  • Set Text property of lblPlayer1 to Player 1: .
  • Set Text property of lblPlayer2 to Player 2: .
  • Make lblInstructionPlayer2 control visible.
  • Disable grpDifficulty .

 

Note that game difficulty levels are only selected when playing against computer (one player).

 

The code to implement these steps is placed into a procedure named rdoPlayer_Click which handles Click events of both rdoOnePlayer and rdoTwoPlayers :

private void rdoPlayer_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    RadioButton ButtonClicked;

    ButtonClicked = (RadioButton) sender;

 

    if (ButtonClicked.Text == "One" )

    {

        NumberOfPlayer = 1;

        lblPlayer1.Text = "You:" ;

        lblPlayer2.Text = "Computer:" ;

        lblInstructionPlayer2.Visible = false ;

        grpDifficulty.Enabled = true ;

    }

 

    else

    {

        NumberOfPlayer = 2;

        lblPlayer1.Text = "Player 1:" ;

        lblPlayer2.Text = "Player 2:" ;

        lblInstructionPlayer2.Visible = true ;

        grpDifficulty.Enabled = false ;

    }

}

 

Add this procedure to your project.

private void rdoDifficulty_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    switch (ButtonClicked.Text)

    {

        case "Easiest" :

            Difficulty = 1;

            break ;

        case "Easy" :

            Difficulty = 2;

            break ;

        case "Hard" :

            Difficulty = 3;

            break ;

        case "Hardest" :

            Difficulty = 4;

            break ;

    }

}

Step 16

You will expand the class definition by adding several methods to help with the animation work. Class methods are used so that objects can do certain jobs. The method is written as a Visual C# method. You will write three methods for the TwoPlayer object, one method that places it on a graphical object, one method that moves it to a new location, and another method that removes it. These three methods are added to the class definition just like the general method when added to the form code file. To add a method to the class description, you choose the name and data type of information that will be generated as a return value. In addition, you specify the arguments required by the method.

 

The Place method places a TwoPlayer object into a graphical object named g (passed as argument):

 

1

2

3

4

5

public void Place(Graphics g)

{

    g.DrawImage( this .MyImage, this .Location);

    this .IsVisible = true ;

}

 

Note the use of this keyword to refer to the current object or the calling object. After the object is placed on g , you set IsVisible property to True .

 

The Move method moves a TwoPlayer object to a new location. The arguments needed are g ( Graphics object), bc ( Brush object) to delete the previous location, dx (change in location x), and dy (change in location y):

 

1

2

3

4

5

6

7

public void Move(Graphics g, Brush bc, int dx, int dy)

{

    g.FillRectangle(bc, this .Location);

    this .Location.X += dx;

    this .Location.Y += dy;

    g.DrawImage( this .MyImage, this .Location);

}

 

The object was deleted first. The location is then updated and the object is redrawn.

 

The Remove method removes a TwoPlayer object from a graphical object (using bc brush):

 

1

2

3

4

5

public void Remove(Graphics g, Brush bc)

{

    g.FillRectangle(bc, this .Location);

    this .IsVisible = false ;

}

using System;

using System.Collections.Generic;

using System.Linq;

using System.Text;

using System.Threading.Tasks;

using System.Drawing;

 

namespace FiringRudal

{

    class TwoPlayer

    {

        public TwoPlayer ()

        {

        }

 

        public Image MyImage;

        public Rectangle Location;

        public bool IsVisible = false ;

 

        public void Place(Graphics g)

        {

            g.DrawImage( this .MyImage, this .Location);

            this .IsVisible = true ;

        }

 

        public void Move(Graphics g, Brush bc, int dx, int dy)

        {

            g.FillRectangle(bc, this .Location);

            this .Location.X += dx;

            this .Location.Y += dy;

            g.DrawImage( this .MyImage, this .Location);

        }

 

        public void Remove(Graphics g, Brush bc)

        {

            g.FillRectangle(bc, this .Location);

            this .IsVisible = false ;

        }

    }

}

TwoPlayer object is placed on a graphical object ( MyImage ) using: MyPlayer.Place (MyImage) . The TwoPlayer object is moved using: MyPlayer.Move(MyImage, MyBrush, dx, dy) , where MyBrush is a solid brush that has the same color as the background color of the graphical object, dx is how far you want to move the object horizontally, and dy is how far you want to move the object vertically.

private void btnGame_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    if (btnGame.Text == "New Game" )

    {

        MyGraphics.Clear(pnlGame.BackColor);

        btnGame.Text = "Stop Game" ;

        btnOption.Enabled = false ;

        btnExit.Enabled = false ;

        Player1Hit = 0;

        Player2Hit = 0;

        lblHitPlayer1.Text = "0" ;

        lblHitPlayer2.Text = "0" ;

        Player1Rem = RudalMax;

        Player2Rem = RudalMax;

        lblRemPlayer1.Text = Player1Rem.ToString();

        lblRemPlayer2.Text = Player2Rem.ToString();

        Player1.Location = new Rectangle(5, ( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Height - 0.5 *

            Player1.MyImage.Height), Player1.MyImage.Width,

            Player1.MyImage.Height);

        Player2.Location = new Rectangle(pnlGame.ClientSize.Width –

            Player2.MyImage.Width - 5, ( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Height - 0.5 *

            Player2.MyImage.Height), Player2.MyImage.Width,

            Player2.MyImage.Height);

        Player1.Place(MyGraphics);

        Player2.Place(MyGraphics);

    }

    else

    {

        Player1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Player2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        btnGame.Text = "New Game" ;

        btnOption.Enabled = true ;

        btnExit.Enabled = true ;

        MyGraphics.DrawString( "Game Over" , new Font( "Arial" , 24),

            Brushes.Yellow, 530, 210);

    }

}

This event can be used to detect keys that are pressed, along with control keys such as Alt, Ctrl, Shift, cursor control, and other control keys. The KeyCode property is a member of the Keys class. There are a number of values ​​for each key that can be pressed. The Intellisense feature of the Visual C# IDE will provide KeyCode values ​​when needed. KeyDown event generally have a Select Case structure with a Case clause for each possible key (or key combination).

 

In this game, you choose the following keys to control the player's movement and to throw rudal (selected from the keyboard):

private void FormFightingPlane_KeyDown( object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

{

    if (btnGame.Text == "New Game" )

        return ;

    switch (e.KeyCode)

    {

        case Keys.A:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y < 0)

                Player1.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.Z:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player1.Location.Height)

                Player1.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player1.Location.Height;

            break ;

        case Keys.K:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y < 0)

                Player2.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.M:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player2.Location.Height)

                Player2.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player2.Location.Height;

            break ;

    }

}

 

Note that you do not allow KeyDown events to occur if the user has not started a game (that is, if btnGame still says New Game ). Add this procedure to your project.

Step 22

In this project, you will give players the ability to throw rudal at each other. Rudal will be represented by Image object just like player. The only difference here is that when rudal is fired, it moves without user interaction at a predetermined speed and its position is updated by the timer control. And, you need to constantly check if the rudal collides with another object. TwoPlayer class does not have properties for speed, or methods that check collisions. So, you need a new class to define rudal.

 

You will explain rudal using MovingRudal class. This class will have a number of properties and methods from TwoPlayer class (using inheritance), plus the speed properties and a method for checking collision. To build this class, you can start from scratch, with all new properties and new methods. Or, you can take advantage of the concept of inheritance in object-oriented programming. Inheritance is a concept where you can build an existing class-based class, by adding its own properties and/or methods. This will save work.

 

You will see how inheritance is used. You will add the collision checking method later. Now, just focus on class properties. Add a class to the project, name it MovinRudal . Use the following class code:

Step 25

Player 1 fires rudal by pressing the S key. Player 2 fires rudal by pressing the J key. You set a number of rules in firing the rudal. First, you will only allow one rudal from each player to be displayed on the screen at a time (no multi pitching). Second, the player cannot throw rudal if he runs out of rations. If these conditions are met, when the player fires rudal, these steps are carried out:

  • Decrease the remaining rudals.
  • Update the remaining rudals.
  • Position the rudal to the side of the player (in the right of player 1, in the left of player 2).
  • Place rudal snowballs on graphic objects using Place method of TwoPlayer class.

        case Keys.A:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y < 0)

                Player1.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.Z:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player1.Location.Height)

                Player1.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player1.Location.Height;

            break ;

 

        case Keys.S:

            if (!Rudal1.IsVisible && Player1Rem > 0)

            {

                Player1Rem--;

                lblRemPlayer1.Text = Player1Rem.ToString();                 

                Rudal1.Location = new

                    Rectangle(Player1.Location.X + 

                    Player1.Location.Width, Player1.Location.Y,

                    Rudal1.MyImage.Width, Rudal1.MyImage.Height);

                Rudal1.Place(MyGraphics);

            }

            break ;

 

        case Keys.K:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y < 0)

                Player2.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.M:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player2.Location.Height)

                Player2.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player2.Location.Height;

            break ;

 

        case Keys.J:

            if (!Rudal2.IsVisible && Player2Rem > 0)

            {

                Player2Rem--;

                lblRemPlayer2.Text = Player2Rem.ToString();

                Rudal2.Location = new

                    Rectangle(Player2.Location.X –

                    Player2.Location.Width, Player2.Location.Y,

                    Rudal1.MyImage.Width, Rudal1.MyImage.Height);

                Rudal2.Place(MyGraphics);

            }

            break ;

    }

}

Step 30

If rudal is fired at or hits a player, another player will get point (a hit). You need a way to check for such collision. Because rectangular region defines moving object here, you need to know what if two rectangular regions intersect. In Visual C#, this test can be performed using ItersectsWith method of Rectangle structure.

 

To see whether the two rectangular regions ( Rectangular1 and Rectangular2 ) intersect, you need to check the Boolean value of Rectangular1.IntersectsWith (Rectangular2) . If the value is True , then an intersection or collision occurs. If False , then there is no collision.

 

Figure 7.17 Both players now throw rudal at each other

 

To use it on this project, you will add a method, Collide , to MovingRudal class. Open MovingRudal.cs file and add the following change:

using System;

using System.Collections.Generic;

using System.Linq;

using System.Text;

using System.Threading.Tasks;

using System.Drawing;

 

namespace FiringRudal

{

    class MovingRudal : TwoPlayer

    {

        public MovingRudal ()

        {

        }

 

        public int XSpeed;

        public int YSpeed;

 

        public bool Collide(Rectangle r)

        {

            return ( this .Location.IntersectsWith(r));

        }

    }

}

 

This method has a rectangular structural argument (r) for checking collision on the MovingRudal object.

 

As an example of using this method, you can check whether Rudal1 collides with Player2 . The resulting Boolean value: Rudal1.Collide(Player2. Location) will be True if a collision occurs. If a collision occurs, you need to clear the rudal and update the thrower's score.

private void timGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    // status of rudal fired by player 1

    if (Rudal1.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal1.Location.X > pnlGame.ClientSize.Width)

        else if (Rudal1.Collide(Player2.Location))

            Player1Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer1.Text = Player1Hit.ToString();

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

    //status of rudal fired by player 2

    if (Rudal2.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, -RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal2.Location.X < 0)

            // past the edge of the panel

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        else if (Rudal2.Collide(Player1.Location))

        {

            Player2Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer2.Text = Player2Hit.ToString();

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

    }

 

    // Checks game status

    if (!Rudal1.IsVisible && Player1Rem == 0 && !Rudal2.IsVisible &&

          Player2Rem == 0)

        btnGame.PerformClick();

}

Step 33

As designed, the players have no protection from rudal except for their ability to go up and down. You will change it. You will create two ufos roaming the playing field. This ufo will stop rudal fired.

 

You will have two ufos, each represented by a MovingRudal object ( Ufo1 and Ufo2 ). The movements will be random, with few restrictions. Add the following form level declarations to your form to declare ufo objects and random number object:

Random MyRandom = new Random();

 

Ufo will follow some rules. Ufo1 will only move vertically on the left side of the playing field, while Ufo2 will only move vertically on the right side of the playing field. The vertical speed will be random between values ​​1 and 4 (you can change it yourself). Ufo can move up and down. If it moves up, it will start from the bottom side of the playing field. If it moves down, it will start from the top side of the playing field.

    try

            "\\plane.ini" );

        rdoEasy.PerformClick();

    else if (Difficulty == 3)

    else

}

Step 36

The speed of the ufo is assigned using a general function, UfoSpeed . As mentioned, you choose this value randomly, between 1 and 4. Speed ​​can be positive (for downward movement) or negative (for upward movement):

 

1

2

3

4

5

6

7

8

9

1011

private int UfoSpeed()

{

    const int SpeedMin = 1;

    const int SpeedMax = 4;

    int Speed;

    Speed = MyRandom.Next(SpeedMax - SpeedMin + 1) + SpeedMin;

 

    if (MyRandom.Next(2) == 0)

        Speed = -Speed;

    return (Speed);

}

 

 

Step 37

The movement of the ufo is updated on the Tick event of timGame timer. For each update, for each ufo, you need to do these steps:

  • Move ufo using YSpeed ​​property.
  • Check whether ufo has come out of the boundary of the game field.
  • If ufo goes out of the boundary of the game field, do this: Calculate new speed; If the speed is positive, position ufo to the top edge of the playing field so that it can move down; If the speed is negative, position ufo to the bottom edge of the playing field so that it can move up;
  • After moving or repositioning the ufo, check whether the fired rudal collides with it. If there is a collision, remove the rudal from the game field.

private void timGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    // Moves ufo

    Ufo1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, Ufo1.YSpeed);

    if (Ufo1.Location.Y < -Ufo1.MyImage.Height ||

        Ufo1.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height)

    {

        // Recalculates speed

        Ufo1.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

 

        if (Ufo1.YSpeed > 0)

            Ufo1.Location.Y = -Ufo1.MyImage.Height;

        else

            Ufo1.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height;

    }

 

    Ufo2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, Ufo2.YSpeed);

    if (Ufo2.Location.Y < -Ufo2.MyImage.Height ||

        Ufo2.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height)

    {

        // Recalculates speed

        Ufo2.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

 

        if (Ufo2.YSpeed > 0)

            Ufo2.Location.Y = -Ufo2.MyImage.Height;

        else

            Ufo2.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height;

    }

 

    // status of rudal fired by player 1

    if (Rudal1.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal1.Location.X > pnlGame.ClientSize.Width)

            // past the edge of the panel

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        else if (Rudal1.Collide(Player2.Location))

        {

            Player1Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer1.Text = Player1Hit.ToString();

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

 

        else if (Rudal1.Collide(Ufo1.Location) ||

            Rudal1.Collide(Ufo2.Location))

        {

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

    }

 

    //status of rudal fired by player 2

    if (Rudal2.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, -RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal2.Location.X < 0)

            // past the edge of the panel

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        else if (Rudal2.Collide(Player1.Location))

        {

            Player2Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer2.Text = Player2Hit.ToString();

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

 

        else if (Rudal2.Collide(Ufo1.Location) ||

            Rudal2.Collide(Ufo2.Location))

        {

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

    }

 

    // Checks game status

    if (!Rudal1.IsVisible && Player1Rem == 0 && !Rudal2.IsVisible &&

          Player2Rem == 0)

        btnGame.PerformClick();

}

Step 39

By using SoundPlayer class, which is located in the using System.Media namespace, you can add sound to this game.

 

The SoundPlayer class is used to play sound represented by wav file. There are a number of wav files provided in the bin\Debug folder in your project:

 

throw.wav

Sound is played when the rudal is fired.

hit.wav

Sound is played when rudal hits a ufo.

ouch.wav

Sound is played when rudal hits a player.

gameover.wav

Sound is played when the game is over.

 

Before playing a sound, a SoundPlayer object needs to be declared using the usual Dim statement:

 

1

SoundPlayer MySound;

 

The object is then constructed using:

 

1

MySound = new System.Media.SoundPlayer(SoundFile)

 

where FileSound is the full path to the wav file that will be played.

 

Sound is loaded into memory using the Load method of SoundPlayer class:

 

1

MySound.Load()

 

You will modify the code to include sounds. Add the following four form-level declarations:

 

1

SoundPlayer SoundThrow, SoundHit, SoundOuch, SoundGameOver;

private void FormFightingPlane_KeyDown( object sender, KeyEventArgs e)

{

    if (btnGame.Text == "New Game" )

        return ;

    switch (e.KeyCode)

    {

        case Keys.A:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y < 0)

                Player1.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.Z:

            Player1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player1.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player1.Location.Height)

                Player1.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player1.Location.Height;

            break ;

 

        case Keys.S:

            if (!Rudal1.IsVisible && Player1Rem > 0)

            {

                SoundThrow.Play();

                Player1Rem--;

                lblRemPlayer1.Text = Player1Rem.ToString();                 

                Rudal1.Location = new

                    Rectangle(Player1.Location.X + 

                    Player1.Location.Width, Player1.Location.Y,

                    Rudal1.MyImage.Width, Rudal1.MyImage.Height);

                Rudal1.Place(MyGraphics);

            }

            break ;

 

        case Keys.K:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, -PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y < 0)

                Player2.Location.Y = 0;

            break ;

        case Keys.M:

            Player2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, PlayerIncrement);

            if (Player2.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                Player2.Location.Height)

                Player2.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height –

                    Player2.Location.Height;

            break ;

 

        case Keys.J:

            if (!Rudal2.IsVisible && Player2Rem > 0)

            {

                SoundThrow.Play();

                Player2Rem--;

                lblRemPlayer2.Text = Player2Rem.ToString();

                Rudal2.Location = new

                    Rectangle(Player2.Location.X –

                    Player2.Location.Width, Player2.Location.Y,

                    Rudal1.MyImage.Width, Rudal1.MyImage.Height);

                Rudal2.Place(MyGraphics);

            }

            break ;

    }

}

private void timGame_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    // Moves ufo

    Ufo1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, Ufo1.YSpeed);

    if (Ufo1.Location.Y < -Ufo1.MyImage.Height ||

        Ufo1.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height)

    {

        // Recalculates speed

        Ufo1.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

 

        if (Ufo1.YSpeed > 0)

            Ufo1.Location.Y = -Ufo1.MyImage.Height;

        else

            Ufo1.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height;

    }

 

    Ufo2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, 0, Ufo2.YSpeed);

    if (Ufo2.Location.Y < -Ufo2.MyImage.Height ||

        Ufo2.Location.Y > pnlGame.ClientSize.Height)

    {

        // Recalculates speed

        Ufo2.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

 

        if (Ufo2.YSpeed > 0)

            Ufo2.Location.Y = -Ufo2.MyImage.Height;

        else

            Ufo2.Location.Y = pnlGame.ClientSize.Height;

    }

 

    // status of rudal fired by player 1

    if (Rudal1.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal1.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal1.Location.X > pnlGame.ClientSize.Width)

            // past the edge of the panel

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        else if (Rudal1.Collide(Player2.Location))

        {

            SoundOuch.Play();

            Player1Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer1.Text = Player1Hit.ToString();

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

 

        else if (Rudal1.Collide(Ufo1.Location) ||

            Rudal1.Collide(Ufo2.Location))

        {

            SoundHit.Play();

            Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

    }

 

    //status of rudal fired by player 2

    if (Rudal2.IsVisible)

    {

        Rudal2.Move(MyGraphics, MyBrush, -RudalSpeed, 0);

        if (Rudal2.Location.X < 0)

            // past the edge of the panel

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        else if (Rudal2.Collide(Player1.Location))

        {

            SoundOuch.Play();

            Player2Hit++;

            lblHitPlayer2.Text = Player2Hit.ToString();

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

 

        else if (Rudal2.Collide(Ufo1.Location) ||

            Rudal2.Collide(Ufo2.Location))

        {

            SoundHit.Play();

            Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        }

    }

 

    // Checks game status

    if (!Rudal1.IsVisible && Player1Rem == 0 && !Rudal2.IsVisible &&

          Player2Rem == 0)

        SoundGameOver.PlaySync();

        btnGame.PerformClick();

}

Step 44

You certainly can't always find a partner to play the game. So why not if computer becomes your opponent? In the one player option, this game can make a computer as player 2.

 

For such computer control, you need to develop rules to be used by computer as opponent. There are two approaches that can be taken in writing code for computer opponent. You can use simple logic, which makes it very easy for human to win game. Or, you can write code with very detailed logic, which can defeat the human brain. With detailed logic, it will be harder for human to win the match. In this game, you will take both approaches. You first develop simple logic by playing a random game. Then, you use the difficulty level selected using the Options button to determine how often you use random logic versus how often you use detailed logic. The selected values ​​are as follows:

 

Difficulty Level

Simple Logic (%)

Detailed logic (%)

Easiest

100

0

Easy

75

25

Hard

50

50

Hardest

25

75

 

So, when the Easiest level is selected, you use 100 percent simple logic during the game. When the Hardest level is selected, you use 75 percent of detailed logic (you can't possibly make the computer too smart, because human will always lose) and 25 percent of simple logic. The movement of the computer will be controlled by a separate timer control ( timComputer ). For easier games, you will create a greater value for the Interval property for this timer. This will slow down the computer process. The interval values ​​selected here:

 

Difficulty Level

Interval

Easiest

1000

Easy

750

Hard

500

Hardest

250

 

So at the Difficult difficulty level, the computer moves four times more often than when the Easiest difficulty level is selected.

 

You will use Integer variable ( RandComputer ) to represent a percentage of the simple logic time used and an Integer variable ( TimeComputer ) to represent the Interval property of the timer control. Add the following form level declarations to the project:

private void rdoDifficulty_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    RadioButton ButtonClicked;

    ButtonClicked = (RadioButton)sender;

 

    switch (ButtonClicked.Text)

    {

        case "Easiest" :

            Difficulty = 1;

            RandComputer = 100;

            TimeComputer = 1000;

            break ;

        case "Easy" :

            Difficulty = 2;

            RandComputer = 75;

            TimeComputer = 750;

            break ;

        case "Hard" :

            Difficulty = 3;

            RandComputer = 50;

            TimeComputer = 500;

            break ;

        case "Hardest" :

            Difficulty = 4;

            RandComputer = 25;

            TimeComputer = 250;

            break ;

    }

    timComputer.Interval = TimeComputer;

}

private void btnGame_Click( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

        lblHitPlayer2.Text = "0" ;

        Player2Rem = RudalMax;

        lblRemPlayer2.Text = Player2Rem.ToString();

        Player1.Location = new Rectangle(5, ( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Height - 0.5 *

            Player1.MyImage.Height), Player1.MyImage.Width,

            Player1.MyImage.Height);

        Player2.Location = new Rectangle(pnlGame.ClientSize.Width –

            Player2.MyImage.Width - 5, ( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Height - 0.5 *

            Player2.MyImage.Height), Player2.MyImage.Width,

            Player2.MyImage.Height);

        Player1.Place(MyGraphics);

        Player2.Place(MyGraphics);

 

        Ufo1.Location = new Rectangle(( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Width - Ufo1.MyImage.Width),

            MyRandom.Next(pnlGame.ClientSize.Height),

            Ufo1.MyImage.Width, Ufo1.MyImage.Height);

        Ufo2.Location = new Rectangle(( int )(0.5 *

            pnlGame.ClientSize.Width),

            MyRandom.Next(pnlGame.ClientSize.Height),

            Ufo2.MyImage.Width, Ufo2.MyImage.Height);

        Ufo1.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

        Ufo2.YSpeed = UfoSpeed();

        Ufo1.Place(MyGraphics);

        Ufo2.Place(MyGraphics);

 

        timGame.Enabled = true ;

 

        if (NumberOfPlayer == 1)

            timComputer.Enabled = true ;

 

        this .Focus();

    }

    else

    {

        timGame.Enabled = false ;

        timComputer.Enabled = false ;

        Player1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Player2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Rudal1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Rudal2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Ufo1.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        Ufo2.Remove(MyGraphics, MyBrush);

        btnGame.Text = "New Game" ;

        btnOption.Enabled = true ;

        btnExit.Enabled = true ;

        MyGraphics.DrawString( "Game Over" , new Font( "Arial" , 24),

            Brushes.Yellow, 280, 160);

    }

}

 

 

Step 46

Now, you will write down the rules of the computer game. You will start with a simple random rule. In this rule, the computer will only move up and down in the game field, and occasionally throw rudal. The only non-random element added is that the computer can only throw rudal if it has at least as many rudals as the player has. This is to prevent the computer from firing all the rudals and becoming an easy target for human. The rules used are:

  • Generate a random value from 0 to 4.
  • If the random value is 0, throw rudal, if computer has at least as many as the remaining rudals owned by the player.
  • If the random value is 1 or 2, move up.
  • If the random value is 3 or 4, make down.

With this rule, rudals are fired one by one in five up or down movements. The computer will move up 2 movements of 5 movements and move down 2 movements from 5 movements.

 

In detailed (smart) logic game rules, you only need to think about how you want to win the game. The smart rule is to throw if other players are "within a certain range". And, avoid human player if he fires rudal. In the rules given here, "in range" means that the vertical difference between two players is not more than 80 percent of the player's height:

 

  • If it is "in range" and the computer has at least as many rudals as the player has, the computer will throw rudal.
  • If the human player fires rudal or the computer no longer has the remaining rudals, the computer will make a defensive move: If human player is above the computer player, the computer will move down; If the human player is below the computer player, the computer will move up.
  • Otherwise, the computer will make an attacking move: If the human player is above the computer player, the computer will move up; If the human player is under the computer player, the computer will move down.

 

Note that the computer can only throw rudal when it has at least as many rudals left as the player has. You certainly don't want a computer to run out of rudals before a human player.

 

The code for both of these logic is placed in the Tick event procedure of timComputer control. Before writing this code, you need to overcome the problem of how you make computer player throw, move up, or move down. With human as the second player, pressing J key will make player 2 throw, K key pressing will make player 2 move up and pressing M key will make player 2 move down. It would be better if there was a way to make the computer press the same key for the job.

 

Fortunately, Visual C# has a procedure named SendKeys that can be used to simulate key presses on the keyboard. To press J key, the code is: SendKeys.Send("K") . Therefore, for computer player, you will use SendKeys procedure to implement computer actions.

 

The Tick event procedure of timComputer control which implements computer player logic is given as follows:

private void timComputer_Tick( object sender, EventArgs e)

{

    int i;

    if (MyRandom.Next(100) < RandComputer)

    {

        i = MyRandom.Next(5); // Moves randomly

        if (i == 0)

        {

            if (Player2Rem >= Player1Rem)

                SendKeys.Send( "J" ); // Fires rudal

        }

        else if (i <= 2)

            SendKeys.Send( "K" ); // Moves up

        else

            SendKeys.Send( "M" ); // Moves down

    }

    else

    {

        if (Math.Abs(Player1.Location.Y - Player2.Location.Y) <

            ( int )(0.8 * Player1.MyImage.Height) && Player2Rem >=

            Player1Rem)

            SendKeys.Send( "J" ); // Fires rudal

        if (Rudal1.IsVisible || Player2Rem == 0)

        {

            if (Player1.Location.Y - Player2.Location.Y < 0)

                SendKeys.Send( "M" ); // Moves up

            else

                SendKeys.Send( "K" ); // Moves down

        }

        else

        {

            if (Player1.Location.Y - Player2.Location.Y < 0)

                SendKeys.Send( "K" ); // Moves up

            else

                SendKeys.Send( "M" ); // Moves down

        }

    }

}
